title: Function mapping
parts: and whose outputs belong to B.
example: f : ℤ → ℤ, f(x) = x + 1 maps each integer to another integer.
note: B is the codomain. The actual outputs (image) need not fill all of B.
wrong: Every element of B must be an output.
f is a set containing A and B.
f always maps B into A.

title: Function composition
parts: Apply f, then apply g to its result,
example: If f(x) = x + 1 and g(x) = 2x, then (g ∘ f)(3) = 8.
note: Read composition from right to left: g(f(x)).
wrong: Apply g first and then f.
Multiply g(x) by f(x).
Add g(x) to f(x).

title: Base ten logarithm
parts: The power that 10 must be raised to
note: A logarithm finds the exponent. It does not ask what number to raise to 100.
wrong: 100 raised to 10 equals 2.
10 multiplied by 100 equals 2.
The square root of 100 is 2.

title: Base two logarithm
parts: The power that 2 must be raised to
note: This appears in binary search: repeated halving leads to logarithmic growth.
wrong: Two raised to the power n.
n divided by 2.
The square root of n.

title: Summation
parts: the value of i each time.
note: The lower limit starts the counter. The upper limit is included.
wrong: Multiply 1, 2, 3 and 4 together.
Add only 1 and 4.
Add i four times, without changing i.

title: Limit of a function
parts: As x gets arbitrarily close to zero
example: For f(x) = x + 2, the limit as x approaches 0 is 2.
note: A limit concerns nearby inputs. f(0) need not even be defined.
wrong: f(0) must equal L and be defined.
x gets arbitrarily large.
f(x) is always exactly L.

title: Derivative
parts: The rate of change with respect to x
example: At x = 3, the slope of y = x² is 6.
note: A derivative describes local slope, not the average change over a whole interval.
wrong: The area under x squared is 2x.
Divide x squared by x to get 2x.
The second derivative of x is 2x.

title: Definite integral
parts: the function f with respect to x.
note: A definite integral gives signed accumulation. Areas below the axis contribute negatively.
wrong: Find the average of f(a) and f(b).
Find the derivative of f at b.

title: Indefinite integral
parts: The family of antiderivatives of f with respect to x.
note: Include the constant C because constants disappear under differentiation.
wrong: One fixed numerical area under f.
The derivative of f with respect to x.

title: Partial derivative
parts: Differentiate f with respect to x while keeping the other independent variables fixed.
note: Holding y fixed does not mean substituting y = 0.
wrong: Differentiate f with respect to all variables at once.
Set x to zero and evaluate f.

title: Gradient
parts: The vector of first partial derivatives of f.
note: The gradient is a vector for a scalar-valued function. The divergence of a vector field is a scalar.
wrong: The sum of all first partial derivatives of f.
The matrix of second partial derivatives.

title: Chain rule
parts: The derivative of the composite at x
is the outer derivative at the inner value
example: If f(u) = u² and g(x) = 3x, the result is 2(3x) × 3 = 18x.
note: Evaluate the outer derivative at g(x), rather than at x.
wrong: Multiply f′(x) by g′(x) for every pair of functions.
Add the outer and inner derivatives.

title: Second derivative
parts: The derivative of the first derivative, evaluated at x.
example: If f(x) = x³, then f′(x) = 3x² and f″(x) = 6x.
note: The double prime means differentiate twice.
wrong: Square the first derivative.
Evaluate the first derivative at twice x.
